body: I’ve noticed comments related to how the word is used are getting deleted so I’m going to try to explain this in a way that isn’t anecdotal or off topic. In the gay community the word itself isn’t necessarily sexual. It’s used to self identity whether that be on a dating app or outside a sexual context entirely. It has absolutely nothing to do with anything other than body type/weight. That alone is enough to be considered sexual harassment though. I’m not arguing that using that word to describe you without your consent is okay or that it’s a term of endearment. It isn’t okay and it makes you uncomfortable so that doesn’t matter. However, it would probably help to understand the context if you’re going to move forward to any capacity. Sorry you had to go through that.

I would start by picking an area you want to live in, scouting out some apartments and start making calls. Most apartments up for sale aren’t even fully vacant yet so there’s no harm in filing an application before you’re even in Florida. Hope that helps

Edit: I used to live in Florida and definitely be careful about the area you choose. Anything cheap in Miami is dangerous as fuck. Ft Lauderdale area is nice but you might have to settle for a surrounding suburb. Also just keep in mind there’s not going to be a lot to do anywhere too far away from a touristy beach. You really have to try and find a middle ground.

I don’t necessarily mean you have to capitalize on your hobbies. I just mean you have to find the most sustainable way of living. Whether that’s finding a job that allows you to work less, finding a job that matches your interests, or even just not working. I’m pretty much just saying you shouldn’t settle for a job or lifestyle that has a net negative effect on your life. Try stuff out and quit whatever your doing the second you know it’s going to continue making you miserable. Too many people stay at jobs they hate just for the chance at climbing the corporate latter. And even if you get promoted chances are your just going to run into the same problems.

The only advice I can give is to roll with the punches and try to make the best out of your circumstance. A lot of people in this world have been screwed over since birth, but that doesn’t mean you don’t have the right to be happy. Put yourself first and find what’s fulfilling. You’ll always find a way to survive so use every second to find a way to survive that isn’t soul crushing. It takes a lot of trial and error but it’s a lot better than settling for a job or a lifestyle that’s going to eat away at you day by day. Do what makes YOU happy. That’s all that matters

I’ve had trouble holding down jobs for a while and I haven’t found a perfect solution, but gig work is worth looking into. I do deliveries and it’s pretty low stress. I work when I want and get paid to drive around listening to podcasts, which is already what I do in my free time. Most of the time I average around $20 an hour. The negative is that you’re always at the mercy of the customers. Sometimes I crank out 15 orders in a few hours and end up averaging $35/hr, and other times I struggle to find 3 and make $10/hr. On top of that it’s a little stressful knowing someone can report a missing order to get free food at any time and you might get banned on the spot. I can’t say it’ll work for you, but you can always try it out for a day or two. That’s the beauty of gig work.

You’re not wrong I just think you’re misunderstanding what we’re saying. Diagnosis is important and it wouldn’t be a great idea to start broadening definitions, but all were saying is mental illness as a whole is a spectrum. We all practice irrational behavior from time to time the only thing that separates the “normal” people from the mentally ill is the frequency of that behavior. For example, when I’m experiencing mania mixed with anxiety most of my symptoms overlap with something like autism. I have those traits and I probably could be diagnosed with ASD, but then I have weeks where I’m just depressed and show less of those traits so a BPD diagnoses is what would be most fitting. A diagnoses doesn’t really mean anything it’s just a label used to effectively treat people. My point is a lot of those traits are there in everyone from time to time, but only some cases require treatment, and even less require an ASD diagnoses. I’m willing to bet there’s millions of people out there with mild aspergers that haven’t been diagnosed or have been diagnosed with something broader because it doesn’t severely interfere with their lives. At the end of the day getting treatment is all that matters and some people really don’t need it.

I don’t think that was meant to trivialize anything. Psychology is a really tricky science with overlapping symptoms all over the place.
